text:
sasha: Heads-up — we're seeing p99 spikes out of AMS POP starting ~16:30 UTC. Baseline throughput OK but tail latency doubled for several routes. Correlates with yesterday's kernel-selector rollout (green). Logs show kernel flip churn + intermittent DNS timeouts to resolver cluster.

sasha: quick grep from infer-worker logs:
```
2026-06-02T16:31:12Z infer-worker[pid]: kernel-selector: chosen=int8_v2 for model=redwood-13b seq=640 latency_est=35ms
2026-06-02T16:31:12Z infer-worker[pid]: kvcache: miss key=batch_prefix_abc size=0
2026-06-02T16:31:12Z network: dns: lookup resolver-ams-1 failed: timeout
2026-06-02T16:31:13Z infer-worker[pid]: kernel-fallback: selected=fp16_v1 fallback_reason=kvcache_cold
```

sasha: not sure if kernel misselect + kv cold misses are compounding with DNS path noise. :thinking_face:

arjun: I ran a quick traceroute from the POP egress host to resolver-ams-1, seeing high RTT on hop 6 -> looks like provider steering upstream change around 16:28 UTC.
```
traceroute to resolver-ams-1 (10.2.6.9), 30 hops max
 1  10.2.0.1  0.2 ms
 2  100.64.0.5  1.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.17  1.8 ms
 4  * * *
 5  203.0.113.33  60.3 ms  <-- big jump
 6  203.0.113.45  120.7 ms <-- provider path
```
arjun: raising with netops to see if upstream provider has any config churn. Also saw ~30% DNS retry rate for that resolver in the last 5m.

claire: chain of causes makes sense. The kernel-selector change (commit abcdef1) modified heuristic to pick int8 kernel whenever seq > 512 and token density < 0.4 — that was supposed to be perf win, but we didn't account for fallback cost when kvcache is cold. When kvcache miss occurs, we do a kernel fallback which is expensive and multiplies latency.

claire: perf-bot profile snapshot for the affected worker (summary):
- cpu sys: +18% on kernel-conversion path
- stall on kvcache miss: 12-25ms per request
- kernel fallback overhead: ~40ms extra (memory reshuffle + recompile path)
Link: https://perf.internal/shot/ams-1768001234 (perf-bot)

perf-bot: quick note — top flame shows heavy time in kernel-selector::choose() and kvcache::lookup() for threads above 50% p99. Cold miss rate jumped after the rollout.

tom: can we triage quick mitigations? I can trigger a rollback of the kernel-selector flag for AMS canary if we decide.

claire: Proposed short-term mitigations (fast):
- rollback kernel-selector change for AMS canary (env flag = selector=stable)
- increase kv warmup for ams pop: preload top prefixes during low traffic (script below)
- pin resolver to alternate provider for POP until netops confirms upstream stability

claire: warmup script (one-off):
```bash
curl -s "https://internal-api/kv/warm?prefix=top-100&pop=ams" || true
# run via cron during 02:00 UTC low-traffic window
```

sasha: +1 on rolling selector back, and pin resolver to 8.8.8.8 for POP temporary. Can someone trigger rollback and route pin? I'll monitor p99 and kv miss rate.

arjun: I can flip resolver to fallback 8.8.8.8 at the POP level and open ticket with provider. Doing it now.

deploy-bot: rollback started: change_id=rlbk-2026-06-02-01, target=kernel-selector, scope=ams-canary, initiated_by=tom

deploy-bot: rollback succeeded: change_id=rlbk-2026-06-02-01, status=completed in 35s

sasha: After rollback + resolver pin, p99 dropped ~30% in the first 2 minutes. kv miss rate also trending down as warmups hit. Will keep monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:

claire: follow-up items: add a canary metric for fallback_count in kernel-selector, add unit test for kvcache interaction in heuristic, and avoid selecting int8 if kvcache_cold_rate > 5% in the same POP. Filing follow-up ticket.

sasha: Thanks team — keeping this thread for postmortem notes. If netops confirms provider churn we may need a broader routing policy for AMS. :eyes:
